transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

For years now I’ve felt this constant heaviness and sadness that never really lifts, even when things in my life are going okay. I've tried to just keep pushing through it, but it has become too hard to ignore.

During these years of feeling down, have there been stretches of 2 months or longer when your mood felt mostly normal? Also, have you had any separate periods when the depression became much worse than your usual baseline for at least 2 weeks?

No, I haven't had any breaks at all—this heavy, low mood has been steady and constant for over three years without ever lifting. It doesn't really come in separate, worse waves either; it just feels like a continuous, heavy baseline that is already quite severe and unchanging every single day.

The patient also denies distinct 2-week periods of worsening beyond baseline, making a separate single depressive episode or recurrent episodic pattern less likely. Therefore the current candidates narrow to [F34.1].

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a chronic depressed mood lasting over three years with no symptom-free interval of 2 months or longer, consistent with persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia). The interview also indicates no distinct superimposed major depressive episodes, supporting dysthymia rather than recurrent episodic depression.
